AAPL.rationale: Apple demonstrates solid fundamental health with strong Q1 FY2026 results (revenue $143.76B, +15.7% YoY; EPS $2.84, +18.3% YoY; operating cash flow $53.92B, +80.1% YoY) and a durable competitive moat built on ecosystem lock-in, 2.5B+ active devices, and a high-margin Services segment growing 14% YoY. The balance sheet is resilient with $88.19B equity and manageable debt ($88.5B, D/E ~1.0). However, the stock trades at a P/E of 34.4x, near the middle of its 30-43x 12-month range, which is not cheap versus its own history given the growth rate. The CEO transition (Tim Cook to John Ternus in September 2026) introduces execution uncertainty, and regulatory headwinds (DOJ antitrust trial, EU DMA) remain material risks. The upcoming Q2 earnings on April 30 could serve as a near-term catalyst — consensus expects $1.93 EPS and $109.35B revenue, with Bank of America and Goldman Sachs forecasting upside. The capital-light AI strategy (only $12.7B capex vs peers' $100B+) preserves financial flexibility but raises questions about long-term AI competitiveness. Net: a quality franchise with solid trajectory, but valuation is fair rather than compelling, and the leadership transition plus regulatory overhang temper conviction.
key_factors: Q1 FY2026 record revenue $143.76B (+15.7% YoY) and EPS $2.84 (+18.3% YoY)

P/E of 34.4x is mid-range (30-43x over past year) — not cheap vs own history for a ~18% EPS grower
CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus (Sept 2026) introduces strategic execution uncertainty
DOJ antitrust trial slated late 2026 and EU DMA compliance risk App Store economics
Q2 earnings April 30 as near-term catalyst — multiple analysts expect upside to consensus $1.93 EPS
Capital-light AI approach ($12.7B capex) preserves cash flow but raises long-term AI competitiveness questions
China iPhone shipments surged 20% YoY in Q1 2026, showing geographic diversification progress
Operating cash flow $53.92B in Q1 alone demonstrates exceptional cash generation capacity
Tariff exposure (~$1.4B/quarter) manageable but cumulative drag on margins over time
